stories.title: Iran targets sites in Bahrain, Kuwait after US strikes
stories.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said they targeted US military sites in Bahrain and Kuwait in the early hours of this morning after the US launched a wave of military strikes on Iran in response to attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz. Iranian media also reported a series of blasts in the port city of Bushehr this morning. Located in Iran's southwest, Bushehr hosts the country's only civilian nuclear power plant and lies near Kharg island, the main oil terminal through which 90% of the nation's crude exports transit. In the latest blow to the fragile ceasefire agreement, the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said it carried out a joint missile ⁠and drone operation against key US military sites in Bandar Salman, Bahrain's Fifth Naval District and Ali Al Salem Air Base in Kuwait.

stories.title: Post-mortem due after woman's body found in Killarney
stories.summary: A post-mortem examination is due to be carried out on the body of a woman discovered at a house in Killarney, Co Kerry, yesterday. She has been named locally as Jamey Carney, who was in her 40s. Ms Carney was found at her home on the Muckross Road yesterday afternoon by a family member, who raised the alarm. It is understood Ms Carney was of American descent and lived in the town for a number of years.

stories.title: Portion of O'Connell Street site acquired for MetroLink
stories.summary: Transport Infrastructure Ireland (TII) has acquired a portion of the Hammerson site on O'Connell Street for the development of MetroLink. The site, which spans around 200 metres along O'Connell Street and is approximately two acres in size, was once home to the Carlton Cinema and had formed part of a €500 million redevelopment plan for the area by the UK-based property group. TII said bringing the site into public ownership is a significant step in facilitating the delivery of MetroLink but will also allow it to work with Dublin City Centre Taskforce on a masterplan for the redevelopment of the capital's main street. A station at O'Connell Street is planned as part of the MetroLink project, but it is not clear what impact this development will have on the wider regeneration of the Dublin Central site owned by Hammerson.

stories.title: Personal injury claims third lower than before pandemic
stories.summary: Two reports released by the Injuries Resolution Board (IRB) show the number of personal injury claims continued to fall last year and is more than a third lower than before the Covid-19 pandemic. Both the IRB Annual Report for 2025 and the latest Personal Injuries Award Values Report for the second half of last year show 20,077 claims were submitted to the board in 2025, which was a 4% drop on 2024 and 35% below 2019 levels. According to the research, the board delivered over €88 million in savings - an increase of €12 million compared to 2024 - through the avoidance of legal costs due to accepted claims not progressing to litigation. The report says the figures "reflect the sustained impact of reforms across the personal injuries landscape".

stories.title: Pace of greenhouse gas emissions reduction too slow - EPA
stories.summary: Ireland's greenhouse gas emissions fell for the fourth consecutive year in 2025, declining by 2.2% to leave emissions 14.5% below 2018 levels, according to new figures from the Environmental Protection Agency. However, the agency warns the pace of reductions remains far too slow to meet the country’s legally binding climate targets for 2030. The EPA said annual emissions need to fall four-and-a-half times faster than they did last year if Ireland is to meet its legally binding climate targets for 2030. The agency warns that achieving this will be extremely challenging.

stories.title: FAI EGM to vote on Israel fixtures at Aviva this evening
stories.summary: The Football Association of Ireland (FAI) will this evening host an Extraordinary General Meeting at Aviva Stadium to vote on a motion regarding the Republic of Ireland's upcoming Nations League fixtures with Israel. As it stands, Heimir Hallgrimsson's team are scheduled to face Israel in Debrecen in Hungary on 27 September for the 'away' tie, before the return 'home' fixture on 4 October in Backa Topola, Serbia. Before the draw was made, last November's FAI general assembly established, with an 89% majority, that the Irish football community felt strongly enough to propose their suspension from European competition due to the war in Gaza and specific breaches of FIFA and UEFA rules Once Ireland were drawn in the same group as Israel, an EGM was proposed by a group including LOI clubs Cork City and Bohemians, the Professional Footballers' Association of Ireland and the Irish Football Supporters’ Partnership, with the specific purpose of voting on a motion calling for a boycott of the two fixtures.
